sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Passaic quickly?
sections.html:
A Passaic owner can put the house on the market, sell it privately, or accept an as-is cash offer, and each route must clear the city's occupancy certificate and fire certification before the closing. The choice comes down to how much time you can give to repairs, showings and a buyer's financing.

Passaic is a dense city, and many of its buildings hold more than one unit. The Census Bureau shows only 23.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so a large share of sellers are landlords of two, three or four family buildings, heirs, or owners of condos and co-ops. Whichever you are, sort these items first:

  • The deed and the block and lot numbers, which every city application asks for.
  • Tenant leases and rent rolls, if any unit is occupied.
  • Mortgage payoff figures and any open municipal charges.
  • The name the buyer will take title in, because Passaic issues the occupancy certificate under the buyer's name.

sections.h2: What should I know about Passaic as a place to sell?
sections.html:
Passaic sits on the west bank of the Passaic River, 10 miles from New York City and 12 miles from Newark Airport. It covers 3.13 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau puts the 2025 population at 71,337, which works out to about 22,500 residents per square mile. Clifton wraps around it on the north, south and west, and six bridges carry traffic across the river toward Wallington, Garfield and Rutherford.

Dutch settlers founded the area in 1679 as Acquackanonk. It became an independent village in 1871 and was chartered as a city in April 1873, growing into a textile and metalworking center. Main Avenue follows the river from Passaic Park to downtown, and Broadway crosses the city east to west. Passaic Park is known for its large park and larger homes in Queen Anne and Tudor styles, along with condominium towers and garden co-ops.

Industry shaped the street grid. The Okonite company ran its wire plant here from 1878 to 1993, supplying insulated cable for early telegraph lines and for Thomas Edison's first generating station in Lower Manhattan, and 36,000 mill workers walked out in the 1926 textile strike. Experimental television broadcasts began from the city in 1931. Passaic Park today holds an Orthodox Jewish community of more than 1,300 families, with over 20 yeshivas and other institutions and many kosher food shops, and Main Avenue reflects a growing Latino population. Older mill-era buildings and two-family houses are common, so sellers should expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at wiring, roofs and basements.

The Passaic City School District runs 17 schools and enrolled about 14,500 students in 2018-19, and Passaic County Community College opened a campus in the city in 2008. Route 21 is the main road, and the Passaic rail station on NJ Transit's Main Line serves Hoboken and Secaucus Junction. Local and Port Authority buses stop at the Passaic Bus Terminal, and jitneys run along Main Avenue.

Passaic is a renter city with large households, and homes that change hands are often multi-unit buildings. The table below shows Census Bureau QuickFacts figures for the whole city.

About 94 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which tells you most households stay put. Language matters here too: 72.3 percent of residents speak a language other than English at home, so bilingual listing and closing documents help.

sections.h2: What does the City of Passaic require before a sale?
sections.html:
Passaic requires an occupancy certificate on a sale, plus a smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification. The one-family application, filed with the Division of Housing under Inspections and Code, asks for the seller's details and the buyer's name, because the certificate is issued to the buyer. Companies buying through an LLC or corporation must supply the registered agent and the certificate of formation.

  • Certificate fee: $65 on the one-family application, with an expedite option at $300.
  • Inspection and violation reports are emailed to both seller and buyer, and extra copies require an OPRA request.
  • Fire Prevention charges $45 for the first smoke and carbon monoxide inspection and $25 for a reinspection.
  • The fire certification stays valid for three months and covers only the buyer named on it.

The fire inspector looks for a smoke detector on each level, detectors and a carbon monoxide alarm outside every sleeping area, working units, and a fire extinguisher within ten feet of the kitchen. A 90-day temporary certification is available when items fail. The city notes that the occupancy certificate says the property meets Passaic's zoning and property maintenance laws and does not replace construction permits or health approvals. Condo, one, two and three family homes all use the fire form.

sections.h2: What state fees and forms apply to a Passaic sale?
sections.html:
New Jersey charges the seller a Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. For a price above $350,000 the bracket runs from $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000 up to $6.05 per $500 over $1,000,000. Below $350,000, the rates are lower: $2.00 per $500 up to $150,000, $3.35 for the next $50,000, and $3.90 up to $350,000.

Exemptions include deeds from an executor to an heir under a will and transfers inside a family between parent and child. A claimed exemption goes on Form RTF-1, which must be notarized and recorded with the deed. The GIT/REP form is also filed with the deed to show whether a nonresident seller must prepay income tax, and the person who signs the deed fills it out.

Flood disclosure became mandatory on March 20, 2024. Because Passaic lies along the river, check the FEMA flood zone for your lot with the DEP Flood Risk Notification Tool and answer the questions on the property condition disclosure statement before the buyer is bound by contract.

sections.h2: How are Passaic property taxes appealed?
sections.html:
Passaic's assessments are set at 100 percent of market value, as in every New Jersey county, and an owner who thinks the figure is too high files with the Passaic County Board of Taxation. The petition on Form A-1 must be received by April 1, or by May 1 where a revaluation or reassessment took place.

The owner carries the burden of showing that the assessment is unreasonable against market value or the district's common level range. Assessments over $1,000,000 may be filed directly with the State Tax Court, and county board decisions can be appealed to the Tax Court within 45 days. Ask the city tax collector for the balance and any open charges before closing.

faqs.q: Who is named on a Passaic occupancy certificate?
faqs.a: The buyer. The city's one-family application states the certificate is issued under the buyer's name, and an LLC buyer must provide its registered agent and certificate of formation.

faqs.q: How much does the Passaic occupancy certificate cost?
faqs.a: The one-family application lists a $65 certificate fee, with an expedite charge of $300 for faster handling.

faqs.q: How long is the fire certification good for?
faqs.a: Three months from approval, and only for the person named on it. A 90-day temporary certification can be issued when the inspection finds problems.

faqs.q: Is the realty transfer fee my cost as the seller?
faqs.a: Yes. New Jersey puts that fee on the seller at deed recording, and it rises by bracket with the sale price.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal an assessment in Passaic?
faqs.a: At the Passaic County Board of Taxation, by April 1 or May 1 after a revaluation. Assessments above $1,000,000 may go straight to the Tax Court.
